description: Soy estudiante de Ingeniería Electrónica adaptada por el desarrollo de software, la lógica y la enfermedad UI. Para esta edición del hackatón está liderando el Reto 9: Armonización de los Hot Spots de MODIS y VIIRS, con el objetivo de desarrollar una web interactiva que unifique registros satelitales y analice incendios forestales. Busco compañeros motivados en Ciencia de Datos, GIS, Frontend UI/UX y Storytelling/Pitch.
summary: FLARE turns 25 years of NASA fire data for Colombia into one comparable record and an early warning for every municipality. MODIS (since 2000) and VIIRS (since 2012) see fire very differently: VIIRS detects about 3.5 times more, so joining them as they come shows a fire boom in 2012 that never happened. We harmonize both sensors into a single scale (validated with 3.2% national error, r = 0.92) and continue seamlessly with NOAA-20 after Suomi NPP stopped in November 2026. The result is a free, bilingual, mobile-friendly website with a fire map, a month-by-month fire calendar and an alert that compares this year with the last 25 for each of Colombia's 1,122 municipalities. It updates itself every day with new NASA satellite data, so mayors, firefighters and communities can see where and when fire happens and prepare before the burning season.
details:
What it does

FLARE answers three questions for any place in Colombia: Where does it burn? When does it burn? Is this year worse than normal?

- Map: a heat map of fire hotspots by municipality and department for any year or month from 2001 to today, with search and a time-travel bar.

- Calendar: every row is a year and every square a month, so the burning season (January–March, 60% of yearly fire) is visible at a glance.

- Alert: compares fire so far this year with the same dates in the previous 25 years, shows a red, yellow or green status, a countdown to the burning season, a ranking of municipalities and prevention advice.

- Data: anyone can upload new NASA FIRMS files and the page processes them in the browser.

How it works

1. We count fire as cell-days on a 0.1° grid (about 11 x 11 km): a cell with fire on a given day counts once, for any satellite. This removes differences in pixel size and number of overpasses.

2. Using 2013–2021, when MODIS and VIIRS flew together, we measured how much more VIIRS sees for each 2° region and month (with statistical shrinkage) and converted the MODIS-only years to the VIIRS scale. Early years with only Terra get an extra correction.

3. Validation: calibrating on 2013–2017 and predicting 2018–2021 from MODIS alone gave 3.2% national error and r = 0.92.

4. Suomi NPP stopped sending data on 2 November 2026. We measured NOAA-20 against Suomi NPP from 2018 to 2026 (factor 1.021, r = 0.998; 1.3% error when tested on 2023–2025) and continue with NOAA-20 with no gap.

5. A GitHub Actions task runs every morning, downloads yesterday's NOAA-20 data from the FIRMS API, processes it with the same engine as the website, checks the result and publishes it.

Benefits

Municipal risk offices, firefighters, environmental agencies and citizens get a long, consistent and free fire history, and a warning before the season starts. The method and code are open and can be reused for any country covered by NASA FIRMS.

Tools

HTML, CSS and JavaScript (Web Workers, IndexedDB), Leaflet and Leaflet.heat, Apache ECharts, Python for data processing and validation, GitHub Pages for hosting and GitHub Actions for the daily update. The site works on phones and computers, in English and Spanish.
